messages.author: cc877dd828c52a1a
messages.subject: ML SEM
parts:
Dear Lavaan Project Team,

 

While working on a multilevel SEM model with Lavaan, we encountered some problems.

 

Background: We run a multigroup SEM model across several countries. The results show that for one of the three latent variables we want to model, two indicators seem to be problematic.

 

Therefore, in the next step we want to find out via multilevel SEM whether these varying effects of individual indicators can be attributed to country differences. In concrete terms, our model looks as follows:

 

solidx <- '

level: 1

  local =~ v212r+v213r+v214r

  global =~ v215r+v216r+v219r

 social =~ v217r+v218r+v220r

  v217r~~v220r

  v219r~~v218r

  v212r~~v213r

level: 2

  local =~ v212r+v213r+v214r

  global =~ v215r+v216r+v219r

  social =~ v217r+v218r+v220r

  v215r~voteshare

  v215r~imm1

  v215r~GDP

  v215r~yearseu

  v219r~GDP  

  v219r~voteshare  

'

 

fit <- sem(model=solidx,data=evsdata_vera, cluster = "country")

summary(fit)

fitMeasures(fit)

 

Even though the model converges, we get the following error message:

In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :

  lavaan WARNING:

    The variance-covariance matrix of the estimated parameters (vcov)

    does not appear to be positive definite! The smallest eigenvalue

    (= -7.463257e+07) is smaller than zero. This may be a symptom that

    the model is not identified.

 

Do you have an idea what is incorrect in our models or what needs to be corrected to eliminate this error? Moreover, some SE could not be computed.

 

All the best and many thanks,

Ann-Kathrin

messages.author: ac9e1459001ea58d
messages.subject: Re: ML SEM
parts:
Dear Ann-Kathrin, 

I don't really see anything wrong with the model (others might!) but maybe we could get some basic troubleshooting out of the way?
  • What kind of sample size?
  • Have you tried using the EM optimizer as discussed here? https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/multilevel.html#convergence-issues-and-solutions
  • Have you tried a simpler model, perhaps with only a single regressor for v215r and v219r?
Possibly you've done all of these things already, just wanted to double-check.

As for the standard errors, that's just a different way of saying there's something wrong with the variance-covariance matrix so that's the same underlying problem, whatever it is.

Best, 
Stijn
